name: intraday_poc-backtest
notes: The intraday BACKTEST as a walk-forward document (ADR-0027): python -m dskit.pipeline walkforward configs/run-backtest.json --asof 2026-08-25 --adapter intraday_poc. Per fold: train each symbol's LSTM on everything up to the cutoff (minus the embargo), forecast the fold's validation window, and let the select-one program pick exactly one symbol per minute — the aggregate objective is the summed realized next-bar log return of those picks. Every trainer param except monitor is pinned identical to the production fit by test_configs.py, which compares the two documents' params dicts whole — so a knob declared on one side only fails there instead of quietly leaving the backtest to prove something about a different model. What else differs by design: the split filters and the walkforward section. KNOWN SKEW, the price of the one exemption: monitor: val_loss here makes every fold ship its best-scoring epoch's weights, while run-train.json declares no monitor (it wires no val_rows, which the engine refuses to monitor without) and ships whichever epoch trains last. total_realized therefore grades a checkpoint-selection procedure the live artifact never receives, and reads high by whatever that selection is worth — twice over, since the rows selected against are also the rows scored (see qhat_aapl). Read it as an upper bound. Closing it means holding a selection split out of the scored window and monitoring on THAT in both documents; until then do not build hyperparameter search on this objective.

bars.notes: Same store as run-train.json — one source of truth for both documents.

window.notes: Identical windowing to the production fit — backtest and live must consume the same features or the backtest proves nothing.

aapl_train.notes: AAPL rows up to the fold's train cut; the embargo band after it belongs to NO split.

aapl_val.notes: The fold's AAPL validation window, starting AFTER the embargo.

qhat_aapl.notes: Fresh weights every fold (expanding train window); per-epoch train/val loss lands in training_curve.json beside the fold's artifact. The curve tracks val_loss whenever val_rows are wired, as they are here; monitor is the separate switch that makes the best-scoring epoch's weights the ones that persist, instead of whichever epoch happens to train last (ADR-0035). Declaring it therefore changes which weights a fold ships, not which objective is measured — drop the line and the fold keeps its final epoch, which is what run-train.json ships (the document notes carry that skew). CAVEAT: aapl_val is both the monitor's validation set AND the set fc_aapl forecasts and select scores into total_realized (the walkforward objective), so best-epoch selection is made against the same rows the fold is graded on — an optimism the objective does not correct for. The fix is a selection split held out from the scored rows; wire one before building hyperparameter search on total_realized. TRADE-OFF: a monitor also makes an EMPTY validation window fatal instead of merely unscored. The engine reads wired-but-empty val_rows as no validation set at all and refuses the fit with 'no val_rows are wired' — a message that misdescribes this wiring — so a fold whose val window falls past the end of the store aborts the whole walk-forward rather than training on and letting the other symbol carry the pick. If the store's tail is short, shorten val_days or re-acquire before running; do not go hunting for a wiring bug. device is declared explicitly as cpu so the compute target is visible in the document — the engine's undeclared default is already CPU (the engine never sniffs a GPU; device is declared, never detected), so this line documents the choice rather than guarding against drift. optimizer_params names Adam's other knobs (weight_decay etc.) explicitly at their library defaults, so the knob is visible and adjustable rather than a silent zero.

qhat_msft.notes: The MSFT twin of qhat_aapl — device/optimizer_params/monitor mirror its rationale: an explicitly documented CPU compute target, Adam's other kwargs named at their library defaults, and best-epoch selection by validation loss (ADR-0035), with the same msft_val-is-also-the-scored-set caveat noted on qhat_aapl.

fc_aapl.notes: One belief per AAPL validation minute — the trainer's signal predicts straight off the fitted module; a row without full feature coverage is skipped, never fabricated.

params.provenance_waiver: rows already carry their symbol; the ports are split by symbol upstream, so a port tag would duplicate the field

forecasts.notes: Both symbols' beliefs in one stream for the selector; key=symbol proves the ports stayed disjoint.

params.provenance_waiver: rows already carry their symbol; the ports are split by symbol upstream, so a port tag would duplicate the field

labeled.notes: The validation rows with their y_next labels — what realizes each pick after the fact.

select.notes: The PoC's one constraint on the PyomoSolve doorway: exactly one symbol per minute, maximize predicted next-bar return. metrics.total_realized — the summed realized log return of the picks — is the walk-forward objective.

walkforward.notes: Three expanding folds over the backfill's tail. Next-bar labels resolve in one minute, so a 1-day embargo is already generous — it exists to keep the discipline visible, not because the label needs it.

outputs.notes: Empty = ./pipeline_runs under the invoking cwd; walkforward writes one full run dir per fold plus the aggregate summary.
